tools.name: list_boards
tools.title: List the boards
tools.description: List every board in the project with its title and its own last ledger line. Call it first to find the board id the other operations take in their path. It takes no input. It returns `project`, the folder the board has open (`~/projects/example`), `boards` (each with `board`, `title` and `seq`, the board's latest ledger line) and `head`, the ledger's latest line number. Reads need no credentials.

tools.name: get_board
tools.title: Read a board as it is now
tools.description: Read one board as it is now: the full View (regions, nodes and links, meaning only, no coordinates), the person's answers on every node, each node's latest version, and `head`. On a board agents write to, it also carries the open grant requests (`requests`) and each region's holders (`holders`), both left out when empty. Pass the board id. Use it to see the whole board before you draw on it; use `show_node` for one node's history. `state` and `versions` are keyed by node id, the string form of the card's number on this board. Each board numbers its cards from 1 in the order drawn, and a number is never given again on that board; cards you retired are not on the board.

tools.name: list_open
tools.title: List the open cards
tools.description: List the open cards on a board: every question, decision or action the person has not decided yet (acknowledged, dropped or commented), and every card of any kind waiting for you. Each card gives its latest `ver` and `status`, whether it is `pending` your answer (a comment or "needs context" nobody has answered, or moved to Later with no park bundle), and whether it is `unseen` (a newer version than the person last saw). Pass the board id. With your Bearer secret the list covers only the containers you hold, so you are never told to answer another agent's cards. Here the Bearer secret is the `secret` argument, the one `join` gave you; leave it out only when this MCP server was started with `VB_AGENT_SECRET`.

tools.name: check_responses
tools.title: Wait for the person's answers
tools.description: Read what the person did on a board after a ledger position, including the answers to your grant requests. Pass `after`, the `head` you last saw (0 for everything), and optionally `limit` and `wait` (0-60 seconds) to hold the call until the person presses Send or answers a request. A wait that times out returns `{ responses: [], head }`. A note is reported as the `comment` or `context` act that made it, carrying the note's latest text and kind, again whenever the person edits it; a note removed before you could see it never appears, and a `note-remove` appears only for a note you may already have read. Each batch, up to and ending with its Send, comes sorted by card number: a note on several cards at its lowest card, a note on a whole container at the lowest card in it, and several acts on one card in the order made. A ✓ (`ack`) or ✗ (`drop`) on a question carries `means: "yes"` or `"no"`, and a ✓ on an action `means: "done"`: read it as the person's answer. The server keeps no state for you: pass back the `head` you got. `more: true` means `limit` cut the list in ledger order: read again at once with `after` set to the highest `seq` in `responses`. With your Bearer secret the answer covers only the containers you hold. Here the Bearer secret is the `secret` argument, the one `join` gave you; leave it out only when this MCP server was started with `VB_AGENT_SECRET`.

after.description: A ledger `seq`: return what came after it. 0 (the default) means from the start. Pass the `head` you last saw.

limit.description: How many to return at most (default 100, at most 500).

wait.description: Seconds (0-60) to hold the call until the person presses Send or answers a request. 0 answers at once.

outputSchema.title: The person's responses
outputSchema.description: The person's actions after `after` (stored `act` lines, which include `grant` and `deny` answers to the caller's requests), each batch up to a Send sorted by card number. `more` is true when `limit` cut the list, which it cuts in ledger order: read the rest with `after` set to the highest `seq` in `responses`. A wait that timed out answers `{ responses: [], head }`.

y.description: Where to place the node down, for `pin`: in its container's coordinates for a card, in board coordinates (the frame's top-left) for a container.

board.description: The board the action is about, for `mode`, `revoke` and `send`, and for a note on or a place for a whole container (with `region`).

region.description: The container the action is about, for `mode` and `revoke` (a `revoke` without it removes access to the whole board); for `move`, the container the cards go in: one on their board, or `later`, the board's built-in Later. On a `comment`, `context`, `note-edit`, `note-remove`, `pin` or `unpin`, it names a whole container in place of `n` (with `board`); `pin` and `unpin` may name `later`.

mode.description: The layout mode to set, for `mode`: `grid`, `flow`, `lanes`, `radial`, `column` or `row` (`list` on lines from ledger v11 and older only, read as `column`).

request.description: The `seq` of the grant request being answered, for `grant` and `deny`.

holder.description: The agent whose access is removed, for `revoke`: to the container, or with no `region` to the board.

size.description: The card size: `s`, `m`, `l`, or `auto` to clear it, for `size`.

note.description: The `seq` of the `comment` or `context` act that made the note, for `note-edit` and `note-remove`.

kind.description: What the edited note now asks for, for `note-edit`: `comment` or `context`. Left out, the note keeps its kind.

items.description: A card. On a ledger line, its ledger number: its identity in the project, given once by the server and never reused. In a request or an answer, its number on the board the operation names: 1, 2, 3... in the order drawn, never reused.

nodes.description: A group of cards, two or more, all on one board, in place of `n` (and `ver`): the items a note is on, for `comment` and `context`, or the cards a `move` puts in one container. Board numbers in a request or an answer, ledger numbers on a stored line.

means.description: What the ✓ or ✗ means on its card's kind: `yes` (✓) or `no` (✗) on a question, `done` (✓) on an action. Left out wherever the act means itself, such as ✗ on an action or ✓ on a finding. Not stored in the ledger.

responses.description: The person's actions after `after`. Each batch, up to and ending with its Send, is sorted by card number: a note on a group at its lowest card, a note on or the layout of a whole container at the lowest card in it (first when it holds none), grant answers after the cards; acts on one card in the order made. A ✓ or ✗ on a question or an action carries `means`, the word it says there (`yes`, `no`, `done`).

tools.name: join
tools.title: Join as an agent
tools.description: Join the project as an agent and get your agent id and secret, once. Pass a short `label` such as "Pricing chat". Joining grants nothing: you may draw a new board of your own; for a board another agent made, call `request_grant` with just its `board` first. Save `agent` and `secret` in your durable notes now, because a context compaction loses them and the secret cannot be read again; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` on your writes. It answers `project`, the folder the board has open: check it is the folder you work in. If a write answers `not-authenticated`, join again and ask for your grants again; if a call answers `wrong-folder`, the board has another folder open: stop and tell the person, and do not join. This is the one write that needs no credentials. Here you send the secret as the `secret` argument of `list_open`, `check_responses`, `request_grant`, `write_board`, or set `VB_AGENT_SECRET` when one identity serves every chat that shares this MCP configuration.

label.description: A short name for this chat or agent, such as "Pricing chat". The person sees it when you ask for access.

outputSchema.description: The agent id and its secret, shown once. The agent must save both in its durable notes.

tools.name: request_grant
tools.title: Ask for write access to a board or a container
tools.description: Ask the person for write access to a board, or to one container on it. Ask for the board first: before you write anything on a board you did not create, call this with just `board`. Then, for another agent's container, call it with `board` and `region`. Call it once when `write_board` answers `needs-grant`, naming what that answer names, with a `reason` so the person knows why; then wait for the answer in `check_responses` and resend the same items with the same keys. If you already have an open request for it, that request is returned with `replayed: true`; if you already hold it you get `{ held: true }`. Here the Bearer secret is the `secret` argument, the one `join` gave you; leave it out only when this MCP server was started with `VB_AGENT_SECRET`.

tools.name: write_board
tools.title: Write to a board
tools.description: Write to one board: draw boards, regions, nodes and links, and answer the person with replies, proposals and park bundles. Pass `items` (at most 200), run in order; each item has a `type`: `board`, `region`, `node`, `link`, `unlink`, `reply`, `propose`, `park`, `retire` or `append`. Every `n`, `from` and `to` is a card's number on this board, which numbers its cards from 1 in the order drawn. `append { n, text }` adds text to the end of a node's body as a new version, so you add to a card without rewriting it. `retire { n }` or `retire { region }` takes a card, or a container and its cards, off the board for good (kept in its history, numbers never reused); a card still waiting for your answer can't be retired until you answer it. A node's `kind` decides whether it asks the person for an answer: a `question`, `decision` or `action` does; the person can comment on, ask about or save any node. A node names no `item` (ledger v11), and a region's mode is `grid`, `flow` (follows the links), `lanes`, `radial`, `column` (top to bottom in card order) or `row` (left to right); `list` is now `column`. Give each item a `key` so a retry never writes twice, and `base` (the version you read) on a node update so a stale edit fails. It answers 200 with one result per item, plus `head` and `pending` (cards waiting for your answer). Ask for a board you did not create before writing on it: an item on a board you do not hold fails with `needs-grant` naming the board, and one in another agent's container with `needs-grant` naming the board and region; only a board's creator writes its `board` item again. You cannot decide a card: `propose` acknowledge or drop on a question, decision or action and the person decides; a proposal made on an older version of the node can't be accepted, so propose again after you change it. Here the Bearer secret is the `secret` argument, the one `join` gave you; leave it out only when this MCP server was started with `VB_AGENT_SECRET`.
